The former used both GLMs and t-tests in an effort to identify statistically significant differences in crime experience between the two cities. The latter developed GLMs for four separate lighting measures and by roadway types. In general, the results showed limited significant findings in terms of correlations between nighttime crimes and lighting. When comparing the after-before LED ratio of ND crime ratios, the results showed that the after-before LED crime ratio in Cambridge was significantly lower than that for Somerville when analyzing the entire nighttime. While indicating no significant correlations between the dimmed lighting levels and nighttime crimes, these findings seemed to suggest that the LED system in Cambridge coincided with decreased nighttime crimes overall, but the decrease was possibly mostly during non-dimmed nighttime periods. This is understandable since the dimmed levels are mostly during low-activity periods for the specific roadway types. When looking at lighting levels, the only significant correlation identified was a positive correlation between average horizontal illuminance and ND crime ratios for local/C3 roads. The correlation suggested that higher horizontal illuminance was correlated with higher ND crime ratios, which is possibly because roadways with higher illuminance levels are more likely due to more commercial developments around them (due to more ambient light) and therefore have more nighttime activities. 4.2.3 Interview Results The results of the interviews are shown below for each of the questions considered. 1. What are the main benefits of adaptive lighting technologies? Adaptive lighting technologies provide several benefits, including energy savings, reduction of light pollution in environmentally sensitive areas, and the ability to tailor lighting to specific needs such as observation slices or curfews. The benefits also extend to preserving dark skies for astronomical observation, extending the life of lighting components, and improving wildlife habitats. Different areas may have different dimming strategies depending on the level of 73 pedestrian activity or specific concerns, such as student housing areas or an observatory. Adaptive lighting can also serve as visual cues for closed areas, reduce air and light pollution, and provide energy savings. 2. What do you think are the main organizational barriers to adoption and implementation? The main barriers to adoption and implementation of new lighting systems are cost, concerns about risk management, resistance from some organizations, and adherence to existing standards and regulations. Educating and involving key stakeholders in the decision-making process can help overcome some of these barriers. Funding, liability concerns, and difficulties with contract negotiation have also been cited as challenges. However, the benefits of energy savings and improved lighting quality can make these systems appealing to city councils and local governments. 3.
